q: A train running at the speed of 60 km/hr crosses a pole in 9 seconds. What is the length of the train?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Speed}} = \left( {60 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \right){\text{m/sec}} = {\frac{{50}}{3}} {\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{Length}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{train}} = \left( {{\text{Speed}} \times {\text{Time}}} \right) \\ & \therefore {\text{Length}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{train}} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{50}}{3} \times 9} \right)m = 150m \end{aligned}$$

q: A train 125 m long passes a man, running at 5 km/hr in the same direction in which the train is going, in 10 seconds. The speed of the train is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Speed}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{train}}\,{\text{relative}}\,{\text{to}}\,{\text{man}} \\ & = {\frac{{125}}{{10}}} {\text{ m/sec}} \\ & = {\frac{{25}}{2}} {\text{ m/sec}} \\ & = {\frac{{25}}{2} \times \frac{{18}}{5}} {\text{ km/hr}} \\ & = 45\,{\text{km/hr}} \\ & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{speed}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{train}}\,{\text{be}}\,x\,{\text{km/hr}}. \\ & \text{Then, relative speed} = \left( {x - 5} \right)\,{\text{km/hr}} \\ & \therefore x - 5 = 45 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 50\,{\text{km/hr}} \end{aligned}$$

q: The length of the bridge, which a train 130 metres long and travelling at 45 km/hr can cross in 30 seconds, is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Speed}} = {45 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = {\frac{{25}}{2}} \,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{Time}} = 30\,{\text{sec}} \\ & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{length}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{bridge}}\,{\text{be}}\,x\,{\text{metres}} \\ & {\text{Then}},\,\frac{{130 + x}}{{30}} = \frac{{25}}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow 2\left( {130 + x} \right) = 750 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 245\,m \end{aligned}$$

q: Two trains running in opposite directions cross a man standing on the platform in 27 seconds and 17 seconds respectively and they cross each other in 23 seconds. The ratio of their speeds is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{speeds}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{two}}\,{\text{tra ins}}\,{\text{be}}\,x\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{and}}\,y\,{\text{m/sec}}\,{\text{respectively}}. \\ & {\text{Then,}}\,{\text{length}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{first}}\,{\text{train}} = 27x\,{\text{metres}}, \\ & {\text{and}}\,{\text{length}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{second}}\,{\text{train}} = 17y\,{\text{metres}}. \\ & \therefore \frac{{27x + 17y}}{{x + y}} = 23 \\ & \Rightarrow 27x + 17y = 23x + 23y \\ & \Rightarrow 4x = 6y \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{x}{y} = \frac{3}{2} \end{aligned}$$

q: A train passes a station platform in 36 seconds and a man standing on the platform in 20 seconds. If the speed of the train is 54 km/hr, what is the length of the platform?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Speed}} = {54 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \,{\text{m/sec}} = 15\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{Length}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{train}} = \left( {15 \times 20} \right){\text{m}} = 300\,{\text{m}} \\ & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{length}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{platform}}\,{\text{be}}\,x\,{\text{metres}} \\ & {\text{Then}},\,\frac{{x + 300}}{{36}} = 15 \\ & \Rightarrow x + 300 = 540 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 240\,{\text{m}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A train 240 m long passes a pole in 24 seconds. How long will it take to pass a platform 650 m long?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Speed}} = {\frac{{240}}{{24}}} \,{\text{m/sec}} = 10\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & \therefore {\text{Required}}\,{\text{time}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\, {\frac{{240 + 650}}{{10}}} \,{\text{sec}}. \\ & = 89\,sec. \end{aligned}$$

q: Two trains of equal length are running on parallel lines in the same direction at 46 km/hr and 36 km/hr. The faster train passes the slower train in 36 seconds. The length of each train is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{length}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{each}}\,{\text{train}}\,{\text{be}}\,x\,{\text{metres}}. \\ & {\text{Then,}}\,{\text{distance}}\,{\text{covered}} = 2x\,{\text{metres}}. \\ & {\text{Relative}}\,{\text{speed}} \\ & = \left( {46 - 36} \right)\,{\text{km/hr}} \\ & = {10 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & = {\frac{{25}}{9}} \,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & \therefore \frac{{2x}}{{36}} = \frac{{25}}{9} \\ & \Rightarrow 2x = 100 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 50 \end{aligned}$$

q: A train 360 m long is running at a speed of 45 km/hr. In what time will it pass a bridge 140 m long?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Formula}}\,{\text{for}}\,{\text{converting}}\,{\text{from}}\,{\text{km/hr}}\,{\text{to}}\,{\text{m/s:}} \\ & X\,{\text{km/hr}} = {X \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \,{\text{m/s}} \\ & {\text{Therefore,}}\,{\text{Speed}} \\ & = {45 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \,{\text{m/sec}} = \frac{{25}}{2}{\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{Total}}\,{\text{distance}}\,{\text{to}}\,{\text{be}}\,{\text{covered}} \\ & = \left( {360 + 140} \right)m = 500\,m \\ & {\text{Formula}}\,{\text{for}}\,{\text{finding}}\,{\text{Time}} \\ & = {\frac{{{\text{Distance}}}}{{{\text{Speed}}}}} \\ & \therefore {\text{Required}}\,{\text{time}} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{500 \times 2}}{{25}}} \right)\,\sec \\ & = 40\,\sec . \end{aligned}$$

q: Two trains are moving in opposite directions @ 60 km/hr and 90 km/hr. Their lengths are 1.10 km and 0.9 km respectively. The time taken by the slower train to cross the faster train in seconds is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Relative}}\,{\text{speed}} = \left( {60 + 90} \right)\,{\text{km/hr}} \\ & = {150 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & = {\frac{{125}}{3}} \,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{Distance}}\,{\text{covered}} \\ & = \left( {1.10 + 0.9} \right)\,km \\ & = 2\,km \\ & = \,2000\,m \\ & {\text{Required}}\,{\text{time}} \\ & = {2000 \times \frac{3}{{125}}} \,{\text{sec}} \\ & = 48\,sec \end{aligned}$$

q: A jogger running at 9 kmph alongside a railway track in 240 metres ahead of the engine of a 120 metres long train running at 45 kmph in the same direction. In how much time will the train pass the jogger?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Speed}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{train}}\,{\text{relative}}\,{\text{to}}\,{\text{jogger}} \\ & = \left( {45 - 9} \right)\,{\text{km/hr}} \\ & = 36\,{\text{km/hr}} \\ & {36 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & = 10\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{Distance}}\,{\text{to}}\,{\text{be}}\,{\text{covered}} \\ & = \left( {240 + 120} \right)\,m \\ & = 360\,m \\ & \therefore {\text{Time}}\,{\text{taken}} \\ & = {\frac{{360}}{{10}}} \,{\text{sec}} \\ & = 36\,{\text{sec}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A 270 metres long train running at the speed of 120 kmph crosses another train running in opposite direction at the speed of 80 kmph in 9 seconds. What is the length of the other train?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Relative}}\,{\text{speed}} \\ & = \left( {120 + 80} \right)\,{\text{km/hr}} \\ & = {200 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & = {\frac{{500}}{9}} \,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{the }}\,{\text{length}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{other}}\,{\text{train}}\,{\text{be}}\,{\text{x}}\,{\text{metres}}{\text{.}} \\ & {\text{Then,}}\,\frac{{x + 270}}{9} = \frac{{500}}{9} \\ & \Rightarrow x + 270 = 500 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 230 \end{aligned}$$

q: A goods train runs at the speed of 72 kmph and crosses a 250 m long platform in 26 seconds. What is the length of the goods train?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Speed}} = {72 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 20\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{Time}} = 26\,{\text{sec}} \\ & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{the }}\,{\text{length}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{train}}\,{\text{be}}\,x\,{\text{metres}}{\text{.}} \\ & {\text{Then}},\,\frac{{x + 250}}{{26}} = 20 \\ & \Rightarrow x + 250 = 520 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 270 \end{aligned}$$

q: Two trains, each 100 m long, moving in opposite directions, cross each other in 8 seconds. If one is moving twice as fast the other, then the speed of the faster train is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{speed}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{slower}}\,{\text{t rain}}\,{\text{be}}\,x\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{Then,}}\,{\text{speed}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{faster}}\,{\text{train}} = 2x\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{Relative}}\,{\text{speed}} = \,\left( {x + 2x} \right)\,{\text{m/sec}} = 3x\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & \therefore \frac{{ {100 + 100} }}{8} = 3x \\ & \Rightarrow 24x = 200 \\ & \Rightarrow x = \frac{{25}}{3} \\ & {\text{So,}}\,{\text{speed}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{faster}}\,{\text{train}}\, = \frac{{50}}{3}\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & = {\frac{{50}}{3} \times \frac{{18}}{5}} \,{\text{km/hr}} \\ & = 60\,{\text{km/hr}} \end{aligned}$$

q: Two trains 140 m and 160 m long run at the speed of 60 km/hr and 40 km/hr respectively in opposite directions on parallel tracks. The time (in seconds) which they take to cross each other, is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Relative}}\,{\text{speed}} = \left( {60 + 40} \right)\,{\text{km/hr}} \\ & = {100 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & = {\frac{{250}}{9}} \,{\text{m/sec}}. \\ & {\text{Distance}}\,{\text{covered}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{crossing}}\,{\text{each}}\,{\text{other}} \\ & = \left( {140 + 160} \right)m = 300\,m \\ & {\text{Required}}\,{\text{time}} \\ & = {300 \times \frac{9}{{250}}} \,{\text{sec}} \\ & = \frac{{54}}{5}\,{\text{sec}} \\ & = 10.8\,{\text{sec}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A train 110 metres long is running with a speed of 60 kmph. In what time will it pass a man who is running at 6 kmph in the direction opposite to that in which the train is going?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Speed}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{train}}\,{\text{relative}}\,{\text{to}}\,{\text{man}} \\ & = \left( {60 + 6} \right)\,{\text{km/hr}} \\ & = 66\,{\text{km/hr}} \\ & = {66 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & = {\frac{{55}}{3}} \,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & \therefore {\text{Time}}\,{\text{taken}}\,{\text{to}}\,{\text{pass}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{man}} \\ & = {110 \times \frac{3}{{55}}} {\text{sec}} = 6\,{\text{sec}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A train travelling at a speed of 75 mph enters a tunnel 3 1 / 2 miles long. The train is 1 / 4 mile long. How long does it take for the train to pass through the tunnel from the moment the front enters to the moment the rear emerges?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Total}}\,{\text{distance}}\,{\text{covered}} \\ & = \left( {\frac{7}{2} + \frac{1}{4}} \right)\,{\text{miles}} \\ & = \frac{{15}}{4}\,{\text{miles}} \\ & \therefore {\text{Time}}\,{\text{taken}} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{15}}{{4 \times 75}}} \right)\,{\text{hrs}} \\ & = \frac{1}{{20}}\,{\text{hrs}} \\ & = \left( {\frac{1}{{20}} \times 60} \right)\,\min \\ & = 3\,\min \end{aligned}$$

q: A train 800 metres long is running at a speed of 78 km/hr. If it crosses a tunnel in 1 minute, then the length of the tunnel (in meters) is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Speed}} = \left( {78 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \right)\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = {\frac{{65}}{3}} \,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{Time = }}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{minute = 60}}\,{\text{second}}. \\ & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{length}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{tunnel}}\,{\text{be}}\,x\,{\text{metres}}. \\ & {\text{Then}},\, {\frac{{800 + x}}{{60}}} = \frac{{65}}{3} \\ & \Rightarrow 3\left( {800 + x} \right) = 3900 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 500 \end{aligned}$$

q: A 300 metre long train crosses a platform in 39 seconds while it crosses a signal pole in 18 seconds. What is the length of the platform?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Speed}} = {\frac{{300}}{{18}}} \,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{50}}{3}\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{length}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{platf orm}}\,{\text{be}}\,x\,{\text{metres}}{\text{.}} \\ & {\text{Then}}, {\frac{{x + 300}}{{39}}} = \frac{{50}}{3} \\ & \Rightarrow 3\left( {x + 300} \right) = 1950 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 350\,m. \end{aligned}$$

q: A train speeds past a pole in 15 seconds and a platform 100 m long in 25 seconds. Its length is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{length}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{train}}\,{\text{be}}\,x\,{\text{metres}} \\ & \,{\text{and}}\,{\text{its}}\,{\text{speed}}\,{\text{by}}\,y\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & Then,\,\frac{x}{y} = 15\,\,\,\,\,\, \Rightarrow \,\,\,\,\,y = \frac{x}{{15}} \\ & \therefore \frac{{x + 100}}{{25}} = \frac{x}{{15}} \\ & \Rightarrow 15\left( {x + 100} \right) = 25x \\ & \Rightarrow 15x + 1500 = 25x \\ & \Rightarrow 1500 = 10x \\ & \Rightarrow x = 150m \end{aligned}$$

q: A train moves past a telegraph post and a bridge 264 m long in 8 seconds and 20 seconds respectively. What is the speed of the train?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{length}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{train}}\,{\text{be}}\,x\,{\text{metres}} \\ & \,{\text{and}}\,{\text{its}}\,{\text{speed}}\,{\text{by}}\,y\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{Then}},\,\frac{x}{y} = 8\,\,\,\,\,\, \Rightarrow \,\,\,\,\,x = 8y \\ & {\text{Now}},\,\frac{{x + 264}}{{20}} = y \\ & \Rightarrow 8y + 264 = 20y \\ & \Rightarrow y = 22 \\ & \therefore {\text{Speed}} = 22\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = {22 \times \frac{{18}}{5}} \,{\text{km/hr}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 79.2\,{\text{km/hr}} \end{aligned}$$

q: How many seconds will a 500 metre long train take to cross a man walking with a speed of 3 km/hr in the direction of the moving train if the speed of the train is 63 km/hr?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Speed}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{train}}\,{\text{relative}}\,{\text{to}}\,{\text{man}} \\ & = \left( {63 - 3} \right)\,{\text{km/hr}} \\ & = 60\,{\text{km/hr}} \\ & = \left( {60 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \right)\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & = \frac{50}{3}\, \text{m/sec} \\ & \therefore {\text{Time}}\,{\text{taken}}\,{\text{to}}\,{\text{pass}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{man}} \\ & = \left( {500 \times \frac{3}{{50}}} \right)\,\sec \\ & = 30\,\sec \end{aligned}$$

q: Two goods train each 500 m long, are running in opposite directions on parallel tracks. Their speeds are 45 km/hr and 30 km/hr respectively. Find the time taken by the slower train to pass the driver of the faster one.
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Relative}}\,{\text{speed}} \\ & = \left( {45 + 30} \right)\,{\text{km/hr}} \\ & = \left(75 \times \frac{5}{18} \right)\, \text{m/sec} \\ & = {\frac{{125}}{6}} \,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{We}}\,{\text{have}}\,{\text{to}}\,{\text{find}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{time}}\,{\text{taken}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{the}} \\ & {\text{slower}}\,{\text{train}}\,{\text{to}}\,{\text{pass}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{DRIVER}}\,{\text{of}}\, \\ & {\text{Th e}}\,{\text{faster}}\,{\text{train}}\,{\text{and}}\,{\text{not}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{complete}}\,{\text{train}}{\text{.}} \\ & \\ & {\text{So,}}\,{\text{distance}}\,{\text{covered = Length}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{slower}}\,{\text{train}}. \\ & {\text{Therefore,}}\,{\text{Distance}}\,{\text{covered = 500}}\,{\text{m}}. \\ & \therefore {\text{Required}}\,{\text{time}} \\ & = {500 \times \frac{6}{{125}}} \\ & = 24\,\sec \end{aligned}$$

q: Two trains are running in opposite directions with the same speed. If the length of each train is 120 metres and they cross each other in 12 seconds, then the speed of each train (in km/hr) is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{speed}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{each}}\,{\text{train}}\,{\text{be}}\,x\,{\text{m/sec}}. \\ & {\text{Then,}}\,{\text{relative}}\,{\text{speed}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{two}}\,{\text{trains}} = 2x\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{So}},\,2x = \frac{{ {120 + 120} }}{{12}} \\ & \Rightarrow 2x = 20 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 10 \\ & \therefore {\text{Speed}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{each}}\,{\text{train}} = 10\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & = {10 \times \frac{{18}}{5}} \,{\text{km/hr}} \\ & = 36\,{\text{km/hr}} \end{aligned}$$

q: Two trains of equal lengths take 10 seconds and 15 seconds respectively to cross a telegraph post. If the length of each train be 120 metres, in what time (in seconds) will they cross each other travelling in opposite direction?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Speed}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{first}}\,{\text{train}} \\ & = {\frac{{120}}{{10}}} \,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & = 12\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{Speed}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{second}}\,{\text{train}} \\ & {\frac{{120}}{{15}}} \,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & = 8\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{Relative}}\,{\text{speed}} = {12 + 8} = 20\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & \therefore {\text{Required}}\,{\text{time}} \\ & = {\frac{{ {120 + 120} }}{{20}}} \,{\text{ sec}} \\ & = 12\,{\text{sec}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A train 108 m long moving at a speed of 50 km/hr crosses a train 112 m long coming from opposite direction in 6 seconds. The speed of the second train is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{speed}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{second}}\,{\text{ train}}\,{\text{be}}\,x\,{\text{km/hr}}. \\ & {\text{Relative}}\,{\text{speed}}\, \\ & = \,\left( {x + 50} \right)\,{\text{km/hr}} \\ & = \left[ {\left( {x + 50} \right) \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \right]\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & = {\frac{{250 + 5x}}{{18}}} \,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{Distance}}\,{\text{covered}} \\ & = \left( {108 + 112} \right) = 220\,m \\ & \therefore \frac{{220}}{{ {\frac{{250 + 5x}}{{18}}} }} = 6 \\ & \Rightarrow 250 + 5x = 660 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 82\,{\text{km/hr}} \end{aligned}$$

q: Two trains are running at 40 km/hr and 20 km/hr respectively in the same direction. Fast train completely passes a man sitting in the slower train in 5 seconds. What is the length of the fast train?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Relative}}\,{\text{speed}} = \left( {40 - 20} \right)\,{\text{km/hr}} \\ & = \left( {20 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \right)\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & = {\frac{{50}}{9}} \,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & \therefore {\text{Length}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{faster}}\,{\text{train}} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{50}}{9} \times 5} \right)\,m \\ & = \frac{{250}}{9}\,m \\ & = 27\frac{7}{9}\,m \end{aligned}$$

q: A train overtakes two persons who are walking in the same direction in which the train is going, at the rate of 2 kmph and 4 kmph and passes them completely in 9 and 10 seconds respectively. The length of the train is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & 2\,kmph = \left( {2 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \right)\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{5}{9}\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & 4\,kmph = \left( {4 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \right)\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{10}}{9}\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{length}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{train}}\,{\text{be}}\,x\,{\text{metres}}\, \\ & {\text{and}}\,{\text{its}}\,{\text{speed}}\,{\text{be}}\,y\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{Then}},\, {\frac{x}{{y - \frac{5}{9}}}} = 9\,{\text{and}}\, {\frac{x}{{y - \frac{{10}}{9}}}} = 10 \\ & \therefore 9y - 5 = x\,{\text{and}}\,10\left( {9y - 10} \right) = 9x \\ & \Rightarrow 9y - x = 5\,{\text{and}}\,90y - 9x = 100 \\ & {\text{On}}\,{\text{solving,}}\,{\text{we}}\,{\text{get}}:\,x = 50 \\ & \therefore {\text{Length}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{train}}\,{\text{is}}\,50\,m \end{aligned}$$

q: Two stations A and B are 110 km apart on a straight line. One train starts from A at 7 a.m. and travels towards B at 20 kmph. Another train starts from B at 8 a.m. and travels towards A at a speed of 25 kmph. At what time will they meet?

q: Two, trains, one from Howrah to Patna and the other from Patna to Howrah, start simultaneously. After they meet, the trains reach their destinations after 9 hours and 16 hours respectively. The ratio of their speeds is:

q: A train running at the speed of 60 kmph crosses a 200 m long platform in 27 seconds. What is the length of the train?

q: A train running at a speed of 90 km/hr crosses a platform double its length in 36 seconds. What is the length of the platform in meters?

q: A train of length 150 meters takes 40.5 seconds to cross a tunnel of length 300 meters. What is the speed of the train in km/hr?

q: A 280 meter long train crosses a platform thrice its length in 50 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/hr?

q: A train 110 meters long is running with a speed of 60 kmph. In what time will it pass a man who is running at 6 kmph in the direction opposite to that in which the train is going?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Speed of train relative to man}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {60 + 6} \right){\text{km/hr}} \\ & = 66\,{\text{km/hr}} \\ & = \left( {66 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \right)m/\sec \\ & = \left( {\frac{{55}}{3}} \right)m/\sec \\ & \therefore {\text{Time taken to pass the man}} \\ & = \left( {110 \times \frac{3}{{55}}} \right)\sec \\ & = 6\,\sec \end{aligned}$$

q: Two trains A and B start running together from the same point in the same direction, at the speed of 60 kmph and 72 kmph respectively. If the length of each of the trains is 240 meters, how long will it take for B to cross train A?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Relative speed}} \\ & {\text{ = (72}} - {\text{60) km/hr}} \\ & {\text{ = 12 km/hr}} \\ & = \left( {12 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \right)m/\sec \\ & = \left( {\frac{{10}}{3}} \right)m/\sec \\ & {\text{Total distance covered}} \\ & {\text{ = Sum of lengths of trains}} \\ & {\text{ = (240 + 240) m}} \\ & {\text{ = 480 m}} \\ & {\text{Time taken}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {480 \times \frac{3}{{10}}} \right)\sec \\ & = 144\sec \\ & = 2\min \,24sec \end{aligned}$$

q: Two trains are moving in opposite directions @60 km/hr and 90 km/hr. Their lengths are 1.10 km and 0.9 km respectively. The time taken by the slower train to cross the faster train in second is?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Relative speed}} \\ & {\text{ = (60 + 90) km/hr}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {150 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \right){\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {\frac{{125}}{3}} \right){\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{Distance coverd}} \\ & {\text{ = (1}}{\text{.10 + 0}}{\text{.9)km}} \\ & {\text{ = 2 km}} \\ & {\text{ = 2000 m}}{\text{}} \\ & {\text{Required time}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {2000 \times \frac{3}{{125}}} \right)\sec \\ & = 48{\text{ sec}}\end{aligned}$$

q: Two trains of lenths 120 m and 90 m are running with speed of 80 km/hr and 55 km/hr respectively towards each other on parallel lines. If they are 90 m apart, after how many seconds they will cross each other?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Relative speed}} \\ & {\text{ = (80 + 55)km/hr}} \\ & {\text{ = 135 km/hr}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {135 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \right)m/\sec \\ & = \left( {\frac{{75}}{2}} \right)m/\sec \\ & {\text{Distance covered}} \\ & {\text{ = (120 + 90 + 90)m}} \\ & {\text{ = 300m}} \\ & {\text{Required time}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {300 \times \frac{2}{{75}}} \right)\sec \\ & = 8\sec \end{aligned}$$

q: Two trains are coming from opposite directions with speed of 75 km/hr and 100 km/hr on to parallel tracks. At some moment the distance between them is 100km. After T hours, distance between them is again 100 km. T is equal to?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Relative speed}} \\ & {\text{ = (75 + 100)km/hr}} \\ & {\text{ = 175 km/hr}} \\ & {\text{Time taken to cover 175 km}} \\ & {\text{at relative speed = 1 hr}} \\ & \therefore {\text{T = Time taken to cover 200 km}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {\frac{1}{{175}} \times 200} \right)\, \text{hr} \\ & = \frac{8}{7}\, \text{hr} \\ & = 1\frac{1}{7}\, \text{hr} \end{aligned}$$

q: A train, 240 m long, crosses a man walking alone the line in opposite direction at the rate of 3 kmph in 10 seconds. The speed of the train is?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Speed of the train relative to man}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {\frac{{240}}{{10}}} \right){\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{ = 24 m/sec}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {24 \times \frac{{18}}{5}} \right){\text{ km/sec}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{{432}}{5}{\text{km/hr}} \\ & {\text{Let the speed of the train be x kmph}}{\text{.}} \\ & {\text{Then relative speed = }}\left( {x + 3} \right){\text{kmph}} \\ & \therefore x{\text{ + 3 = }}\frac{{432}}{5} \\ & \Rightarrow x = \frac{{432}}{5} - 3 \\ & \Rightarrow x = \frac{{417}}{5} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 83.4\,{\text{kmph}} \end{aligned}$$

q: Two trains of equal length are running on parallel lines in the same directions at 46 km/hr and 36 km/hr. The faster train passes the slower train in 36 seconds. The length of each train is?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let the length of each train be }}x{\text{ metres}} \\ & {\text{Then distance covered}} \\ & {\text{ = 2x metres}} \\ & {\text{Relative speed}} \\ & {\text{ = (46}} - {\text{36)km/hr}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {10 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \right)m/\sec \\ & = \left( {\frac{{25}}{9}} \right)m/\sec \\ & \therefore \frac{{2x}}{{36}} = \frac{{25}}{9} \Leftrightarrow 2x = 100 \Leftrightarrow x = 50 \end{aligned}$$

q: Two trains of equal lengths takes 10 seconds and 15 seconds respectively to cross a telegraph post. If the length of each train be 120 miters, in what time ( in seconds) will they cross each other traveling in opposite direction?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Speed of the train}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {\frac{{120}}{{10}}} \right){\text{ m/sec}} \\ & {\text{ = 12 m/sec}} \\ & {\text{Speed of the second train}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {\frac{{120}}{{15}}} \right){\text{ m/sec}} \\ & {\text{ = 8 m/sec}} \\ & {\text{Relative speed}} \\ & {\text{ = (12 + 8)m/sec}} \\ & {\text{ = 20 m/sec}} \\ & \therefore {\text{Required time}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{{\left( {120 + 120} \right)}}{{20}}\,\sec \\ & = 12\,\sec \end{aligned}$$

q: A train B speeding with 120 kmph crosses another train C running in the same direction, in 2 minutes. If the lengths of the trains B and C be 100m and 200m respectively, what is the speed (in kmph) of the train C?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Relative speed of the trains }} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {\frac{{100 + 200}}{{2 \times 60}}} \right){\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {\frac{5}{2}} \right){\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{Speed of train B}} \\ & {\text{ = 120 kmph}} \\ & = \left( {120 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \right){\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {\frac{{100}}{3}} \right){\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{Let the speed of second train be }}x{\text{ m/sec}} \\ & {\text{Then, }} \frac{{100}}{3} - x = \frac{5}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow x = \left( {\frac{{100}}{3} - \frac{5}{2}} \right) \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \left( {\frac{{185}}{6}} \right){\text{m/sec}} \\ & \therefore {\text{Speed of second train}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {\frac{{185}}{6} \times \frac{{18}}{5}} \right){\text{ kmph}} \\ & {\text{ = 111 kmph}} \end{aligned}$$

q: What is the speed of a train if it overtakes two persons who are walking in the same direction at the rate of a m/s and (a + 1) m/s and passes them completely in b seconds and (b + 1) seconds respectively?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let the length of the train be }}x{\text{ metres}} \\ & {\text{and its speed be }}y{\text{ m/s}} \\ & {\text{Then,}} \\ & {\text{ }}\frac{x}{{y - a}}{\text{ = b}}\,\,{\text{and}}\, \\ & \,\frac{x}{{y - \left( {a + 1} \right)}} = \left( {b + 1} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow {\text{ }}x{\text{ = }}b\left( {y - a} \right){\text{ and}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{ }}x = \left( {b + 1} \right)\left( {y - a - 1} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow b\left( {y - a} \right) = \left( {b + 1} \right)\left( {y - a - 1} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow by - ba = by - ba - b + y - a - 1 \\ & \Leftrightarrow y = \left( {a + b + 1} \right) \end{aligned}$$

q: A train passes a 50 meter long platform in 14 seconds and a man standing on platform 10 seconds.The speed of the train is?

q: Two trains start simultaneously (with uniform speeds) from two stations 270 km apart, each to the opposite station; they reach their destinations in $$6\frac{1}{4}$$ hours and 4 hours after they meet. The rate at which the slower train travels is :
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Ratio of speeds}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\sqrt 4 :\sqrt {6\frac{1}{4}} \\ & = \sqrt 4 :\sqrt {\frac{{25}}{4}} \\ & = 2:\frac{5}{2} \\ & = 4:5 \end{aligned}$$ Let the speeds of the two trains be 4x and 5x km/hr respectively Then time taken by trains to meet each other $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{ = }}\left( {\frac{{270}}{{4x + 5x}}} \right){\text{hr}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {\frac{{270}}{{9x}}} \right){\text{hr = }}\left( {\frac{{30}}{x}} \right){\text{hr}} \\ & {\text{Time taken by slower train to travel}} \\ & {\text{ 270 km = }}\left( {\frac{{270}}{{4x}}} \right){\text{hr}} \\ & \therefore \frac{{270}}{{4x}} = \frac{{30}}{x} + 6\frac{1}{4} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{270}}{{4x}} - \frac{{30}}{x} = \frac{{25}}{4} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{150}}{{4x}} = \frac{{25}}{4} \\ & \Rightarrow 100x = 600 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 6 \\ & {\text{Hence speed of slower train}} \\ & {\text{ = 4}}x \\ & = \,24\,{\text{km/hr}} \end{aligned}$$

q: Two trains, A ans B start from stations X and Y towards each other, they take 4 hours 48 minutes and 3 hours 20 minutes to reach Y and X respectively after they meet. If train A is moving at 45 km/hr, then the speed of the train B is?

q: A train takes 9 sec to cross a pole. If the speed of the train is 48 kmph, then length of the train is?

q: Two trains start at the same time from A and B and proceed toward each other at the sped of 75 km/hr and 50 km/hr respectively. When both meet at a point in between, one train was found to have traveled 175 km more then the other. Find the distance between A and B?

q: Two trains 180 meters and 120 meters in length are running towards each other on parallel tracks, one at the rate 65 km/hr and another at 55 km/hr. In how many seconds will they be cross each other from the moment they meet?

q: A train running at the speed of 84 km/hr passes a man walking in opposite direction at the speed of 6 km/hr in 4 seconds. What is the length of train (in meter)?

q: A train passes two bridges of length 500 m and 250 m in 100 seconds and 60 seconds respectively. The length of the train is?

q: Train A passes a lamp post in 3 seconds and 900 meter long platform in 30 seconds. How much time will the same train take to cross a platform which is 800 meters long? (in seconds)

q: A train cover a distance of 3584 km in 2 days 8 hours. If it covers 1440 km on the first day and 1608 km on the second day, by how much does the average speed of the train for the remaining part of the journey differ from that for the entire journey?

q: Train A traveling at 63 kmph can cross a platform 199.5 m long in 21 seconds. How much would train A take to completely cross (from the moment they meet ) train B, 157 m long and traveling at 54 kmph in opposite direction which train A is traveling? (in seconds)
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Speed of train A}} \\ & {\text{ = 63 kmph}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {\frac{{63 \times 5}}{{18}}} \right){\text{m/sec}} \\ & {\text{ = 17}}{\text{.5 m/sec}} \\ & {\text{Speed of train B}} \\ & {\text{ = 54 kmph}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {\frac{{54 \times 5}}{{18}}} \right){\text{m/sec = 15 m/sec}} \\ & {\text{If the length of train A be }}x{\text{ metre,}} \\ & {\text{then}} \\ & {\text{Speed of train A}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{{{\text{Length of train + length of platform}}}}{{{\text{Time taken in crossing}}}}{\text{ }} \\ & \Rightarrow 17.5 = \frac{{x + 199.5}}{{21}} \\ & \Rightarrow 17.5 \times 21 = x + 199.5 \\ & \Rightarrow 367.5 = x + 199.5 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 367.5 - 199.5 \\ & \Rightarrow 168\,{\text{metres}} \\ & {\text{Relative speed}} \\ & {\text{ = ( Speed train A + Speed train B)}} \\ & {\text{ = (17}}{\text{.5 + 15) m/sec}} \\ & {\text{ = 32}}{\text{.5 m/sec}} \\ & {\text{Required time}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{{{\text{ Length of train A + Length of train B}}}}{{{\text{Relative speed }}}} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{168 + 157}}{{32.5}}} \right){\text{seconds}} \\ & = 10\,{\text{seconds}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A train which is moving at an average speed of 40 km/h reaches its destination on time. When its average speed reduces to 35 km/h, then it reaches its destination 15 minutes late. The distance traveled by the train is?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Average speed of train}} \\ & {\text{ = 40 km/hr}} \\ & {\text{Reach at its destination at on time }} \\ & {\text{New average speed of train}} \\ & {\text{ = 35 km/h}} \\ & {\text{Time = 15 minutes}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{ = }}\frac{{15}}{{60}}{\text{hours }} \\ & {\text{Then distance travelled}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{{40 \times 35}}{{40 - 35}}{\text{ }} \times \frac{{15}}{{60}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{{40 \times 35}}{5}{\text{ }} \times \frac{{15}}{{60}} \\ & {\text{ = 70}}\,{\text{km}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A train moves with a speed of 30 kmph for 12 minutes and for next 8 minutes at a speed of 45 kmph. Find the average speed of the train?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Distance = Speed }} \times {\text{Time}} \\ & {\text{Distance covered by train with the}} \\ & {\text{speed of 30 kmph in 12 minutes is }} \\ & {\text{ = 30}} \times \frac{{12}}{{60}} = 6{\text{km}} \\ & {\text{Distance covered by the same train}} \\ & {\text{with the speed of 45 kmph in 8 minutes is }} \\ & {\text{ = 45}} \times \frac{8}{{60}} = 6{\text{km}} \\ & {\text{Average speed}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{{{\text{total distance}}}}{{{\text{total time}}}}. \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{\left( {6 + 6} \right){\text{km}}}}{{\left( {12 + 8} \right)\min }} = \frac{{12}}{{20}} \times 60 \\ & {\text{ = 36 kmph}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A man sitting in a train is counting the pillars of electricity. The distance between two pillars is 60 meters, and the speed of the train is 42 km/hr. In 5 hours, how many pillars will he count?

q: A 120 meter long train is running at a speed of 90 km/hr. It will cross a railway platform 230 m long in :

q: A 50 meter long train passes over a bridge at the speed of 30 km per hour. If it takes 36 seconds to cross the bridge, what is the length of the bridge?
s: Speed = $$\left( {30 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \right)$$ m/sec = $$\frac{{25}}{3}$$ m/sec Time = 36 second Let the length of the bridge be x meters. Then, $$\frac{{50 + {\text{x}}}}{{36}}$$ = $$\frac{{25}}{3}$$ ⇒ 3(50 + x) = 900 ⇒ 50 + x = 300 ⇒ x = 250 meters

q: A train takes 5 minutes to cross a telegraphic post. Then the time taken by another train whose length is just double of the first train and moving with same speed to cross a platform of its own length is :
s: Let the length of the train be x metres. Time taken to cover x meters = 5 min = (5 × 60) sec = 300 sec Speed of the train = $$\frac{{\text{x}}}{{300}}$$ m/sec Length of the second train = 2x meters Length of the platform = 2x meters ∴ Required time $$\begin{aligned} & = \left[ {\frac{{2{\text{x}} + 2{\text{x}}}}{{\left( {\frac{{\text{x}}}{{300}}} \right)}}} \right]{\text{sec}} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{4{\text{x}} \times 300}}{{\text{x}}}} \right){\text{sec}} \\ & = 1200\,{\text{sec}} \\ & = \frac{{1200}}{{60}}\,{\text{min}} \\ & = 20\,{\text{minutes}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A train passes a station platform in 36 seconds and a man standing on the platform in 20 seconds. If the speed of the train is 54 km/hr, what is the length of the platform?
s: Speed = $$\left( {54 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \right)$$ m/sec = 15 m/sec Length of the train = (15 × 20) m = 300 m Let the length of the platform be x meters Then, $$\frac{{{\text{x}} + 300}}{{36}}$$ = 15 ⇒ x + 300 = 540 ⇒ x = 240 meters

q: A train speeds past a pole in 20 seconds and speeds past a platform 100 meters in length in 30 seconds. What is the length of the train?
s: Let the length of the train be x meters and its speed be y m/sec. Then, $$\frac{{\text{x}}}{{\text{y}}}$$ = 20 ⇒ y = $$\frac{{\text{x}}}{{20}}$$ ∴ $$\frac{{{\text{x}} + 100}}{{30}}$$ = $$\frac{{\text{x}}}{{20}}$$ ⇒ 30x = 20x + 2000 ⇒ 10x = 2000 ⇒ x = 200 meters

q: The time taken by a train 180 m long, travelling at 42 kmph, in passing a person walking in the same direction at 6 kmph, will be
s: Speed of train relative to man = (42 - 6) kmph = 36 kmph = $$\left( {36 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \right)$$ m/sec = 10 m/sec ∴ Time taken to pass the man = $$\frac{{180}}{{10}}$$ sec = 18 sec

q: Two trains 200 meters and 150 meters long are running on parallel rails in the same direction at speed of 40 km/hr and 45 km/hr respectively. Time taken by the faster train to cross the slowed train will be:
s: Relative speed = (45 - 40) km/hr = 5 km/hr = $$\left( {5 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \right)$$ m/sec = $$\frac{{25}}{{18}}$$ m/sec Total distance covered = Sum of lengths of trains = (200 + 150) m = 350 m ∴ Time taken = $$\left( {350 \times \frac{{18}}{{25}}} \right)$$ sec = 252 seconds

q: A train with 90 km/hr crosses a bridge in 36 seconds. Another train 100 meters shorter crosses the same bridge at 45 km/hr. What is the time taken by the second train to cross the bridge?
s: Let the lengths of the train and the bridge be x meters and y meters respectively. Speed of the first train = 90 km/hr = $$\left( {90 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \right)$$ m/sec = 25 m/sec Speed of the second train = 45 km/hr = $$\left( {45 \times \frac{5}{{18}}} \right)$$ m/sec = $$\frac{{25}}{2}$$ m/sec Then, $$\frac{{{\text{x}} + {\text{y}}}}{{36}}$$ = 25 ⇒ x + y = 900 ∴ Required time $$\begin{aligned} & = \left[ {\frac{{\left( {{\text{x}} - 100} \right) + {\text{y}}}}{{\frac{{25}}{2}}}} \right]{\text{sec}} \\ & = \left[ {\frac{{\left( {{\text{x}} + {\text{y}}} \right) - 100}}{{\frac{{25}}{2}}}} \right]{\text{sec}} \\ & = \left( {800 \times \frac{2}{{25}}} \right){\text{sec}} \\ & = 64\,{\text{sec}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A train 125 m long passes a man, running at 5 kmph in the same direction in which the train is going, in 10 seconds. The speed of the train is:
s: Speed of the train relative to man $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{125}}{{10}}{\text{m/sec}} \\ & = \frac{{25}}{2}{\text{m/sec}} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{25}}{2} \times \frac{{18}}{5}} \right){\text{m/sec}} \\ & = 45\,{\text{km/hr}} \end{aligned}$$ Let the speed of the train be x kmph. Then, relative speed = (x - 5) kmph ∴ x - 5 = 45 or x = 50 km/hr

q: A train 75 m long overtook a person who was walking at the rate of 6 km/hr in the same direction and passed him in $$7\frac{1}{2}$$ seconds. Subsequently, it overtook a second person and passed him in $$6\frac{3}{4}$$ seconds. At what rate was the second person travelling?
s: Speed of the train relative to first man $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{75}}{{7.5}}{\text{m/sec}} = 10\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & = \left( {10 \times \frac{{18}}{5}} \right){\text{km/hr}} = 36\,{\text{km/hr}} \end{aligned}$$ Let the speed of the train be x km/hr. Then, relative speed = (x - 6) km/hr ∴ x - 6 = 36 ⇒ x = 42 km/hr Speed of the train relative to second man $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{ = }}\frac{{75}}{{6\frac{3}{4}}}\,{\text{m/sec}} \\ & = \left( {75 \times \frac{4}{{27}}} \right){\text{m/sec}} \\ & = \frac{{100}}{9}{\text{m/sec}} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{100}}{9} \times \frac{{18}}{5}} \right){\text{km}} \\ & = 40\,{\text{km/hr}} \end{aligned}$$ Let the speed of the second man be y kmph. Then, relative speed = (42 - y) kmph ∴ 42 - y = 40 ⇒ y = 2 km/hr

q: Two trains are running in opposite directions with the same speed. If the length of each train is 120 meters and they cross each other in 12 seconds, then the speed of each train (in km/hr) is?
s: Let the speed of each train be x m/sec. Then, relative speed of the two trains = 2x m/sec So, 2x = $$\frac{{120 + 120}}{{12}}$$ ⇒ 2x = 20 ⇒ x = 10 ∴ Speed of each train = 10 m/sec = $$\left( {10 \times \frac{{18}}{5}} \right)$$ km/hr = 36 km/hr

q: A 150 m long train crosses a milestone in 15 seconds and a train of same length coming from the opposite direction in 12 seconds. The speed of the other train is?
s: Speed of first train = $$\frac{{150}}{{15}}$$ m/sec = 10 m/sec Let the speed of second train be x m/sec Relative speed = (10 + x) m/sec ∴ $$\frac{{300}}{{10 + {\text{x}}}}$$ = 12 ⇒ 300 = 120 + 12x ⇒ 12x = 180 ⇒ x = $$\frac{{180}}{{12}}$$ = 15 m/sec Hence, speed of other train = $$\left( {15 \times \frac{{18}}{5}} \right)$$ kmph = 54 kmph

q: A man standing on a platform finds that a train takes 3 seconds to pass him and another train of the same length moving in the opposite direction takes 4 seconds. The time taken by the trains to pass each other will be :
s: Let the length of each train be x meters Then, speed of first train = $$\frac{{\text{x}}}{3}$$ m/sec Speed of second train = $$\frac{{\text{x}}}{4}$$ m/sec ∴ Required time $$\begin{aligned} & = \left[ {\frac{{{\text{x}} + {\text{x}}}}{{\left( {\frac{{\text{x}}}{3} + \frac{{\text{x}}}{4}} \right)}}} \right]{\text{sec}} \\ & = \left[ {\frac{{2{\text{x}}}}{{\left( {\frac{{7{\text{x}}}}{{12}}} \right)}}} \right]{\text{sec}} \\ & = \left( {2 \times \frac{{12}}{7}} \right){\text{sec}} \\ & = \frac{{24}}{7}{\text{sec}} \\ & = 3\frac{3}{7}{\text{sec}} \end{aligned}$$
